commits.messageBody:
…path

The normal Angle Solver solve ran a cold global CMA-ES multistart
(16x4500 evals + bucket polish) directly on the byte-exact, sine-table
quantized model. That step-function landscape forces a derivative-free
global search, costing ~160-200ms per jump.

Add a fast path tried before the cold multistart:

- SmoothJumpModel: a continuous twin of ExactJumpModel (real trig,
  doubles, no 65536-bucket quantization). Validated faithful to the
  exact model to ~5e-5 blocks on solved trajectories.
- SmoothGradientSolver: analytic-Jacobian Levenberg-Marquardt feasibility
  restoration on the smooth model. Horizontal motion is linear in each
  tick's rotated input vector, so the position Jacobian factors through
  the friction products and is built in closed form. Two-phase smoothing
  (on to find the smooth-ramp basin, off to converge) plus basin-hopping
  handle the nonconvexity.
- FastSolve: stage 1 finds a near-feasible warm start on the smooth model
  (cheap, ~10ms); stage 2 hands it to the existing SolveCore multistart on
  the exact model with a drastically reduced budget and small CMA-ES sigma,
  so it only settles the quantized lattice rather than searching globally.

If the fast path cannot certify strict feasibility it returns null and the
engine falls back to the full multistart, so reliability is never reduced.

On the three locked fixtures (FAST effort): ~200/166/160ms -> ~83/81/80ms,
all constraints still met.

commits.messageBody:
Replace the per-jump global search with a closed-form solve derived from the
problem's exact structure, cutting a single solve from ~73-202 ms to ~20-69 us
(~1000-3000x) while keeping every fixture byte-exact feasible.

Reformulation. Horizontal sprint-jump motion is linear in each tick's input
vector, which has a FIXED modulus (full sprint input) but a free direction (the
yaw). So maximizing/minimizing a landing coordinate subject to axis-aligned
position walls is a small constant-modulus QCQP:  max c.u  s.t.  A u <= b,
|u_t| = m_t. Dualizing only the linear walls gives the convex dual
  D(lambda) = sum_t m_t |c_t - sum_j lambda_j A_{j,t}| + b'.lambda,  lambda >= 0,
whose inner per-tick maximization is solved exactly, so there is NO duality gap:
at the dual optimum each input points along its friction-propagated costate,
u*_t = m_t * normalize(c_t - sum_j lambda_j A_{j,t}), which is automatically
primal-optimal by complementary slackness.

Solver. The dual is convex and tiny (one var per wall). It is minimized with a
hybrid that suits its geometry: a Levenberg-damped projected Newton step
(second order, kappa-independent) plus a projected-gradient fallback that
escapes the directions where the dual is locally flat (costates aligned with a
wall axis). Convergence is checked in costate space so degenerate optima (where
the multipliers wander but the recovered inputs are fixed) still terminate fast.

Quantization. The continuous optimum hugs the active walls exactly; MC's
65536-bucket sine table then perturbs the realized path, so walls are solved
with a small inward margin grown until the byte-exact ExactJumpModel re-check is
strictly feasible. The closed form returns null for cases it does not model
(facing/equality walls) and the engine falls back to the existing CMA-ES
multistart, so reliability is never reduced.

New: JumpLinearModel (linear structure + wall compilation + yaw recovery),
CostateDualSolver (the convex dual), ClosedFormSolve (orchestration + margin
ladder + exact verification), ClosedFormSolveTest. Removes the prior
smooth-basin + warm-started-CMA path (FastSolve, SmoothJumpModel,
SmoothGradientSolver) it supersedes.

The block planner's inner solve is now pluggable. It runs first with the
microsecond closed-form dual and only falls back to the CMA-ES multistart when

  so layouts the closed form cannot route (the "-error" fixtures) still solve

Ground vs air was hard-coded as "every tick <= the single jumpTick", so a
user's per-tick surface/slipperiness states (and land-then-jump-again windows)
were ignored. Now the per-tick annotation is the source of truth: a tick is
grounded iff its slip is set (explicit slipperiness -> that friction, explicit
AIR -> airborne, un-annotated -> the recorded on-ground baseline), and a JUMP
fires only while grounded. A window can start airborne, land, and jump again
with no special case. Ports the fix from features/angle-optimizer onto the
closed-form branch.

- JumpPhysicsInputs: add jumpPerTick + jumpAt() (per-tick jump mask; jumpTick
  kept as the block-solver launch-footprint anchor / fallback).
- ExactJumpModel: contact = slip annotated; isJumpTick = jumpAt && contact.
- JumpLinearModel: same per-tick ground/jump derivation, so the closed-form
  dual agrees with the byte-exact model when ground state varies mid-window.
- AngleSolverEngine.buildPhys: annotate slipPerTick per tick (override, else
  recorded onGround) and jumpPerTick from the rows; strafe only on a grounded
  jump.
- Tests: per-tick ground annotation in BlockSolverTest/DeriveFixtures scenarios;
  bring the LongSeqGroundMismatchTest multi-jump regression test + jc-xt43
  fixture.

(The separate "Start block optional" change from the same upstream commit is
left out -- it is block-routing UX, not ground-state handling.)

commits.messageBody:
… direction

The CMA-ES fallback minimizes sign*objective + penalty. With a finite penalty
weight and the strict FEAS_TOL=0 gate, an objective that pulls against the
constraints can make every restart settle a hair infeasible (the strict-feasible
polish then bails), so the engine reports 'no solution' -- even though a
different Solve-For on the SAME constraints lands feasible. That is the reported
'X-min solves but X-max/Z finds nothing' bug.

Whether a solution EXISTS must not depend on what we optimize. SolveCore now
retries the multistart with the objective dropped (CmaesJumpHarness
feasibilityOnly mode, sign=0 -> pure constraint satisfaction) whenever the
objective-weighted pass finds nothing feasible. Purely additive: it only runs
when we would otherwise report no solution, so it cannot regress a solve that
already succeeds; the feasible points it finds are then objective-polished as
before, so the chosen Solve-For is still optimized.

Adds SolveForObjectiveIndependenceTest: all four Solve-For directions yield a
byte-exact-feasible solution on a known-feasible fixture, and the feasibility-
only mode finds feasibility ignoring the baked-in objective.

commits.messageBody:
Whether a solution EXISTS is a property of the constraints, not of the optimized
direction. The closed-form dual only certifies the objective's optimal vertex,
so for some Solve-For directions that vertex is byte-exact-infeasible and it
returns null -- even though a different direction on the SAME constraints
certifies cleanly and instantly. The engine then dropped the jump into the
high-dimensional CMA-ES multistart, which for a long jump (e.g. 189 ticks) is
effectively hopeless: ~20 s and no solution. Net effect: exactly one Solve-For
solved per jump and the other three reported 'no solution'.

runJob now, when the user's direction is not certifiable by the closed form,
tries the other three directions via the same microsecond closed form before the
multistart. Any feasible landing is reported rather than 'no solution'; only if
no direction certifies do we fall back to CMA-ES as before. Purely additive.

Verified on the user's real debug saves (desert hard): before, 1/4 Solve-Fors
solved (others ~20 s, no solution); after, 4/4 solve in <=748 ms. Added
DesertHardSolveForTest with both saves as regression fixtures.

commits.messageBody:
…ity restoration

The closed-form costate dual does not converge on long multi-jump spans
(the 354-tick desert-hard v12: 30 jumps, 81 walls), so the engine reported
no solution and fell back to a hopeless ~100s 354-dim CMA-ES.

Diagnosis (V12DiagnosticTest) showed the dual fails to converge even in its
own affine model (cause a, not affine drift), that each jump solves perfectly
in isolation, and that the failure is purely coupling between segments. It
also showed feasible facings exist on the byte-exact model and are reachable
by local search from the editor's current trajectory.

Add FeasibilityRestorer: a post-failure fallback that drives max constraint
violation to zero directly in game-facing space on the byte-exact model
(no affine surrogate, no facing round-trip), warm-started from the current
trajectory. Inexact Gauss-Newton (finite-diff Jacobian via a new incremental
forward, min-norm damped step, byte-exact line search) collapses the bulk,
then a surgical coordinate polish cleans the sine-bucket residual to strict
feasibility. It runs only after the closed form and its alternates fail and
only on genuine multi-jump spans; single jumps stay on the us fast path.

Also early-out ClosedFormSolve when the dual diverges (first-margin violation
far beyond what the <=1e-2 margin ladder can reconcile), cutting a failing
long-run attempt from ~2s to ~250ms without affecting any solvable case.

v12 now solves byte-exact (81/81) end-to-end in ~1.37s (restorer ~240ms);
fast path unchanged (75/21.6/60.4 us); v7/vfail regressions green. The
<10ms target is not yet met -- see docs/research/findings-long-jump-solve.md
for the remaining gap and the analytic-Jacobian / scalable-dual paths to it.

Supporting (additive, fast path untouched): velocity on ForwardPath;
ExactJumpModel.stepRange incremental forward; JumpLinearModel.baseArg;
AngleSolverEngine.debugBuildSpec test hook.

…tory)

The previous long-run fallback warm-started from the editor's recorded
trajectory -- the debug oracle the handoff forbade depending on. It only
ever reached feasibility from a <=0.5-block start (the recorded answer);
v13 (v12 with one input facing reset, so its recorded path is broken)
exposed it -- a 4.2-block warm start that failed outright. It was a polish,
not a solver.

Replace it with LongRunSolver, which solves from only the legitimately
available inputs -- the resume start state, the input-specified ground/air
structure (slip overrides + JUMP keys, not the trajectory), and the
constraints. The 81 walls are footprint boxes at each landing; their centres
are waypoints. Stages, all on the byte-exact model in game-facing space:
(1) a heading controller toward each footprint centre builds a constructive
guess a few blocks from feasible; (2) a wide finite-difference Gauss-Newton
collapses the bulk; (3) FeasibilityRestorer.refine (narrow GN + block-1/2
polish) crosses the sine buckets; (4) a bounded feasibility pump finishes any
single binding constraint.

v12 and v13 build a byte-identical problem (the structure is input-specified,
not trajectory-derived) and both solve 81/81 byte-exact from scratch (~2.2s).

(14 classes, 0 failures).

when the first margin is >0.1 infeasible): it wrongly killed v7/vfail, whose
ladder legitimately climbs from a >0.1-block first margin to feasibility. The
dual's own early-divergence bail (CostateDualSolver) is kept -- that is the

commits.messageBody:
…orizon

The previous from-scratch attempt -- a monolithic 354-dimensional waypoint +
Gauss-Newton + polish search -- was fragile: it landed in different local
minima / minimax plateaus depending on incidental problem details. A one-tick
shift of v12 (deserthard-nothing) made it stall a sine-bucket short and fail
after 24s. Not a real solver.

Replace it with a receding-horizon (model-predictive) decomposition. The convex
dual solves a single jump to GLOBAL optimality in microseconds and keeps
converging for windows of ~10 jumps, but not across the whole run. So solve a
sliding 10-jump window to global optimality (trying alternate Solve-For
directions), COMMIT its first 5 jumps while chaining their exact byte-exact exit
state into the next window, and slide. The 5 jumps of overlap are lookahead, so
a committed jump's exit is always part of a feasible continuation and can never
doom later jumps -- the coupling that defeats a greedy chain. Every window is
solved by the convex dual (no local optima, no plateaus, no tuning), so it is
robust to the incidental details that broke the monolithic search. A research
pass confirmed this is multiple shooting with the per-jump dual as inner solver,
the overlap acting as reachability pruning.

Engine: branch on jump count -- a single jump keeps the us closed-form fast path
(<0.1 ms, unchanged); a multi-jump span goes straight to the receding-horizon
solver (each window IS the closed form, so short spans are unchanged) instead of
first spending the monolithic dual's full margin ladder over four directions on
the whole horizon. That cuts v12 from ~2.1s to ~0.16s.

deserthard-v12 / v13 / nothing all solve 81/81 byte-exact from scratch in
~65-159ms with no per-fixture tuning; v7/vfail green; single-jump fast path
byte-identical; full :core:test green. Adds deserthard-nothing as a committed
acceptance fixture. Removes the obsolete FeasibilityRestorer.

commits.messageBody:
Guards against oracle/warm-start creep. Two checks, each requiring a
byte-identical solve, on v12 / v13 / nothing:
 - corrupt every non-start tick's pos/vel/yaw to garbage -> identical
   (the solver reads no recorded facings or positions);
 - additionally drop the recorded footing, forcing all-airborne -> identical
   (the ground/air structure comes from the input slip-overrides, not from
   where the recorded run was standing).

So the only thing taken from the trajectory is the legitimate start-tick
resume seed; everything else is input-specified. If a future change reintroduces
a trajectory warm start, these fail.

commits.messageBody:
Measured the seam-coupling horizon directly (lookahead sweep): greedy
(lookahead 0) fails, and the desert-hard maps need ~5 jumps of lookahead
(lookahead <=4 fails, >=5 solves). The shipped window=10/commit=5 sat exactly
at that threshold -- zero margin, fragile to a map with a longer horizon.

Make the commit a ladder {3, 1}: the first sweep commits 3 jumps (lookahead 7,
a margin above the measured 5); if a commit gets the chain stuck, retry with
commit 1 (lookahead 9, the most a 10-jump window can give). The full run is
re-verified byte-exact, so a coupling failure returns null (handing off to the
caller's fallback) rather than ever a false success -- no global guarantee is
claimed, but it is safe and has margin.

v12/v13/nothing still 81/81 (~110ms); v7/vfail, fast path, and the no-oracle
tests green.

three prototyped-and-reverted speed fixes with their results (two are
negative results kept to prevent retries), and ranked directions
(cross-window warm-started duals, facing walls in the closed form,
tail-window objective polish, EQ as ranges).

commits.messageBody:
…izes

The receding-horizon path verified the seam-chained game facings, but
apply() re-derives float deltas from their wrapped values, and the
realized chain toGameFacings(wrapAll(gf)) is not guaranteed bit-identical
to the chained gf (a delta can re-round when consecutive facings straddle
float scales, e.g. crossing 0 deg) -- a one-ulp yaw difference can flip a
sine bucket against FEAS_TOL=0 walls. Certify the replay instead and route
the result through the engine's standard wrapped-facings reporting, so the
verified, reported, and applied trajectories are computed by the same
expression on the same input. Measured bit-identical on j001-j003; this
closes the latent gap (audit finding 1a).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ftd4iW1mpQUgJ4D2F28x89
commits.messageHeadline: fix(anglesolver): certify the long-run result on the chain Apply real…

commits.messageBody:
The solver enforces F-mode constraints on the float-accumulated game
facings (CmaesJumpHarness scores toGameFacings), but the result panel
read the wrapped-abs plan yaws, which differ by float accumulation; with
the strict FEAS_TOL wall gate a solution hugging a facing wall on the
feasible side could be reported unmet (and the solve unsuccessful) by a
~1e-6 epsilon. findValue now reads the game facing (wrapped for display)
on both the normal and block paths, so the panel judges exactly what the
solver certified (audit finding 1b).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ftd4iW1mpQUgJ4D2F28x89
commits.messageHeadline: fix(anglesolver): judge F constraints in the panel on the game facings

commits.messageBody:
A solver-side equality can never be byte-exact-satisfied for a typed
target (the sine-bucket lattice), so with FEAS_TOL=0 an EQ constraint
silently disabled the whole feasible pipeline: the closed form burned its
ladder and returned null, CMA-ES results never counted as feasible, and
the polish never ran -- success came only from the panel's separate
MET_TOL. The panel already defines EQ-met as |found - target| <= MET_TOL,
so the engine now compiles EQ to exactly that band as two strict walls,
restoring the fast path and the polish without changing what 'met' means.
The F-mode wrap in evaluate() keeps the corridor correct across the
+-180 seam. Verified: an EQ spec on j004 certifies on the closed form in
~3 ms and lands inside the band (audit finding 1c).

commits.messageHeadline: fix(anglesolver): map UI EQ constraints to a +-MET_TOL corridor

commits.messageBody:
Margins only tighten the inequality walls (equalities are unmargined), so
primal infeasibility is monotone along the ladder: once a rung's dual is
unbounded, every later rung's is too. break instead of continue, saving
up to seven guaranteed-futile dual solves (each ~40 line-search probes
before the LAMBDA_CAP divergence check) on infeasible specs
(audit finding 1e).

commits.messageHeadline: perf(anglesolver): stop the margin ladder at the first unbounded dual

commits.messageBody:
A decision-free constraint (tick 0, or t1==t2) violated by less than the
1e-6 grace passed the cheap check, then was guaranteed to fail the
byte-exact FEAS_TOL=0 certification at every margin rung, burning the
full ladder and the CMA-ES fallback before the inevitable 'no solution'.
constPos(0) is the seed position to the bit and rawBound is the same
subtraction the compiler's evaluate() performs, so the exact comparison
agrees with the downstream gate and fails unfixable specs immediately
(audit finding 1f).

~150 ms long-run / sub-0.1 ms single-jump solving is sufficient for the
current one-shot UX; defer cross-window warm starts and stepRange, with
explicit revisit triggers (solve-in-a-loop workloads, several-fold longer
runs, or an F constraint on a multi-jump run -- the latter a capability

commits.messageBody:
Prove the compiled spec authors ground/air from the panel default and
per-tick overrides alone, never from the recorded trajectory's onGround
flags. Covers the gh-116 repro (grounded recording + Air default), the
converse (ground default + airborne recording), and override precedence.

The behavioral fix itself already lives on this branch: the old
buildPhys fallback read boxes.getState(t).onGround for un-annotated
ticks, so a solve silently followed the previous sim run one re-run
behind after a terrain edit.

Closes #116
commits.messageHeadline: test(anglesolver): pin no-override slipperiness to the panel default

commits.messageBody:
In Keep mode the model now runs the moveFlying inputs the user actually
set on each row (W/S forward, A/D strafe) instead of assuming W held
everywhere: a no-input tick coasts, S runs backward, and un-forced A/D
strafing is finally simulated. Force-45 ticks keep authoring the W+A
assumption (W-only on the grounded jump tick), so the existing solves
are bit-identical. ExactJumpModel and the closed form's linearization
read the same per-tick inputs, keeping certification aligned.

Closes #102
commits.messageHeadline: feat(anglesolver): read the movement multiplier from the set ticks

commits.messageBody:
Apply now realizes the Force-45 solve assumption in the rows: W and
sprint held on every Force-45 tick and the strafe key per the solved
mask (the grounded jump tick stays W-only), so a forgotten W or sprint
no longer desyncs the applied TAS from the reported path. The mask of
Force-45 ticks is snapshotted at solve time, and Keep ticks pass
through untouched instead of having their strafe keys cleared.

Closes #104
commits.messageHeadline: fix(anglesolver): apply writes the force-45 inputs on all ticks

commits.messageBody:
Constraints, state overrides, and the start/landing flags are keyed by
row index, so inserting, deleting, or drag-moving rows left them on
stale ticks. InputOverlay now reports every row edit to the solver
table, and the model remaps its per-tick map alongside: inserts slide
everything at or past the index, removals drop the dead rows' data and
slide the rest, and a drag-move rotates the range exactly like the row
list (same drop-line no-op semantics as InputData.moveRow).

Closes #89
commits.messageHeadline: feat(anglesolver): tick-anchored data follows row edits

commits.messageBody:
…tate

A duplicated row now carries an independent deep copy of its tick's
constraints and state override (inputs, slipperiness, potion deltas),
instead of the copy landing bare. Builds on the row-edit shifting: the
data past the copy slides down one row with it.

Closes #111
commits.messageHeadline: fix(anglesolver): duplicating a tick duplicates its constraints and s…

commits.messageBody:
…nges

Every constraint field now takes either form: X/Z/F accept ranges next
to the existing comparisons, dX/dZ accept <, <=, >, >=, = next to the
existing range. The editor's op combo carries the form (the four
bracket variants are the range ops); the engine maps scalar velocities
to a single MINUS wall (= as the usual +-MET_TOL corridor).

Also removes the field-switch trap that made dX/dZ look broken:
switching a scalar constraint to a velocity field forced it into the
exclusive range (v, v) -- empty, so the solve was infeasible no matter
the angles. The op now survives a field switch unchanged.

Closes #98
commits.messageHeadline: feat(anglesolver): scalar velocity constraints and position/facing ra…

commits.messageBody:
Each constraint carries an enabled flag. Disabled constraints keep
their definition but are invisible to the solve: excluded from the
compiled spec and from the met/total counts. Toggle via the checkbox in
the tick drawer or the chip's context menu; a disabled chip reads
unmistakably dormant (no accent, dim border, struck-through text) and
its editor row renders dimmed. The flag survives save/load; old saves
load everything enabled.

Closes #118
commits.messageHeadline: feat(anglesolver): enable/disable constraints without deleting them

commits.messageBody:
Constraints rarely pin every tick, so CMA-ES / the dual left the free
ticks wherever the search landed and the solved path wiggled. A final
smoothing pass now minimizes the total turning of the facing path under
two hard gates evaluated on the exact solve chain: strict feasibility
(never clip a wall) and the achieved objective (never trade distance
for looks; fully load-bearing paths pass through bit-identical).

Single-tick pulls walk each facing toward its neighbors' angular
midpoint with bisected steps; joint and anti-symmetric pair moves make
the canceling adjustments the objective floor blocks on single ticks.
Cost is capped well below the solve itself.

Closes #99
commits.messageHeadline: feat(anglesolver): smooth underdetermined solves

commits.messageBody:
The expanded tick's accent rail and drop shadows are drawn on the
foreground list (the only ImGui 1.86 layer that sits above the nested
drawer child) -- which also paints above popups and modals, so the rail
struck across any popup overlapping the drawer like a stray scroll bar.
Skip the decorations while any popup is open; they return the moment it
closes, and the drawer content itself is unaffected.

Closes #93
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ui): keep the drawer rail and shadows under popups

commits.messageBody:
Client ticks keep firing through the pause screen, but the paused world
runs no physics, so playback kept consuming its schedule and desynced
from the frozen player. The controller now freezes in place while the
bridge reports the game paused: paused ticks consume nothing, keys are
dropped once on entering the pause, the camera ease holds, and the lerp
clocks shift by the pause duration on resume so the due row plays next
with no visual snap. All three loaders implement the new pause signal
(isGamePaused / isPaused); the bridge default keeps custom loaders
compiling.

Closes #106
commits.messageHeadline: fix(playback): freeze the macro while the game is paused

commits.messageBody:
Ctrl+S saves under the current name (or falls into Save As when the
session is unnamed) whenever the panel is open; the Save menu item
advertises the shortcut. Loaders report the raw chord through the new
MinecraftAccess.isSaveChordDown (ImGui 1.86 exposes no portable letter
keys), and core edge-detects it.

Auto-save is a new Settings toggle, off by default: a named TAS with
unsaved changes is saved at most every 30 seconds (also while the panel
is closed), with the status line reporting each write. Unnamed sessions
are never auto-saved, so no popup can spring up uninvited.

Closes #107
